title: Google Ads vs. Yelp Ads in 2025: Which Platform Wins?

facts.fact: Google Ads charges on a cost-per-click basis, and the article says CPC for high-value industries such as law firms or insurance often soars past $50 per click.
facts.quote: industries with high customer value, like law firms or insurance, often see CPC soar past $50 per click

facts.fact: According to the article, advertisers selling home decor or fitness gear on Google Ads might pay just a few dollars per click.
facts.quote: if you’re selling home decor or fitness gear, you might pay just a few dollars per click

facts.fact: On Yelp Ads, the article says restaurants might pay under $1 per click, while legal services can exceed $50 per click.
facts.quote: restaurants might pay under $1 per click, while legal services can exceed $50

facts.fact: The article states that some businesses start Yelp Ads with as little as $5 per day.
facts.quote: Some businesses start with as little as $5 per day.

facts.fact: On Yelp Ads, advertisers set a daily budget, and actual costs fluctuate with competition and demand.
facts.quote: You set a daily budget, but costs fluctuate based on competition and demand.

facts.fact: Google Local Service Ads operate on a pay-per-lead model, according to the article.
facts.quote: these ads appear at the top of local search results and operate on a pay-per-lead model.

facts.fact: Google Ads uses a pay-per-click model in which advertisers only pay when someone clicks their ad, and Google runs an auction to decide which ads appear.
facts.quote: It works on a pay-per-click model, meaning you only pay when someone interacts with your ad.
